title: Connection
description: What one attempt to reach a tenant turned out to be. WHY THIS IS A CONTRACT, HAVING BEEN ARGUED NOT TO BE. The first version of `connect` published this shape and declared it deliberately unversioned, on the reasoning that a session ends when the process does and therefore has no document to version. That reasoning answered the wrong question. Persistence is not the test; DEPENDENCE is. A consumer already parses this to decide whether a collection may be started, and a shape somebody depends on is a contract whether or not it is called one — the only difference being whether it can change without anybody noticing. IT DESCRIBES AN ATTEMPT AND NOT A RESOURCE, and that is why it is a contract of its own rather than a corner of the evidence. Nothing here is evidence about a tenant: no rule reads it, no assessment carries it, and it produces no finding. It is the answer to a question asked before any evidence exists — can this application registration reach this tenant, and as whom.

$schema.description: The exact contract this document claims, which must be the $id of the schema validating it. An instance convention and not the dialect keyword.

reach.description: How the attempt ended, in four words rather than a boolean. `established` is a session that opened. `refused` is THE TENANT ANSWERING AND DECLINING — consent that was never granted, or the wrong tenant — and `unreachable` is nothing answering at all, or a local environment that cannot try. Those two are different sentences to somebody holding an application registration, and collapsing them sends a person to check their network when the answer was consent. `cancelled` is stopped deliberately, and it is never inferred from an exit code: a sign-in abandoned at a browser and one killed by a network exit identically, and only the caller knows which happened.

attempted_at.description: When the attempt started. Wall clock, because a reader compares it against a sign-in log somebody else is holding.

seconds.description: How long it took, on a monotonic clock. A device-code sign-in waits for a person, so this is mostly a measure of them rather than of the network.

exit_code.description: What the process returned. Published because it is a fact and consumed as a verdict by nobody: `reach` is the answer, and this is the raw reading it was formed from.

requested.description: What was asked, as it was asked. Separate from what came back, and it is the half that survives a total failure: an attempt that reached nothing still knows what it was pointed at and with which application.

session.description: What signing in established, and null when nothing did. Required and nullable rather than optional: null says no session opened, and an absent key would say nothing at all.

because.description: The observable facts that produced the verdict, in the order they were established, and including the collector's own last words on a failure. Never empty: a verdict with nothing behind it is the message this product exists to stop shipping.

asked.description: The addresses and the application. All four keys always, with nulls rather than omissions: an absent key and a null would make 'not supplied' and 'not applicable' read alike.

tenant_url.description: The admin centre. One of the two addresses is required, and which one is a property of what the caller intends to do next.

client_id.description: The Entra ID application registration. Required, because PnP.PowerShell has shipped no application of its own since 2.12.0. A public identifier that authorises nothing on its own.

device_login.description: Whether the code flow was used, for a host with no browser. A fact about how somebody signed in, not about what they could see.

addressResolution.description: WHICH DIRECTORY OWNS AN ADDRESS. A different question from which directory a session operated in, and the reason this document has two blocks rather than one field. Answerable by anybody, from public OpenID discovery, with no token and no application registration: measured against a real tenant with an empty credential cache, and separately against the discovery endpoint itself with no authorization header. It is therefore AUTHORITATIVE ABOUT AN ADDRESS and is not an observation by any identity. Resolved before the sign-in and reported whatever the sign-in does, because a tenant that refuses you still has an address and knowing which directory you were pointed at is most of a consent diagnosis.

host.description: The SharePoint host, normalised. An endpoint rather than an identity, and null where nothing was resolved at all — a collector that never ran read no address, and echoing back the one that was asked for would put a request where a reader expects a result. What was asked is in `requested`.

resolved_tenant_id.description: The directory that owns the host, or null where it could not be resolved. TWO HOSTS THAT RESOLVE HERE TO ONE VALUE ARE ONE ORGANISATION, which is what stops a multi-geo estate reading as several. It is not evidence that anybody reached either of them, and it must never be copied into a field meaning what a collection observed.

how.description: Named rather than implied. A consumer deciding what this value may be used for needs to know it came from a lookup anybody can perform, and a field that left the method to be assumed would eventually be read as an observation.

detail.description: Why it did not resolve. A host that does not exist fails with a reason rather than resolving to nothing.

authenticatedSession.description: WHAT SIGNING IN ESTABLISHED. Read from the connection itself rather than restated from the arguments: the point of connecting is to find out, and echoing back what was asked would answer a different question. NOTHING THAT COULD BE A CREDENTIAL IS HERE, and the omission is deliberate rather than incidental: the underlying connection object also exposes a client secret, a certificate and a credential, and a document that carried one would put it into a terminal, a log, and whatever captured that log.

identity_kind.description: Which kind of identity looked, in the evidence contract's vocabulary so that one word means one thing across the product. Interactive and device sign-in are both delegated: the session sees what one person sees, and the difference changes what an empty result means.

connection_type.description: What the connection calls itself. A fact reported rather than interpreted; nothing in this engine decides anything from it.

scopes.description: The permissions the session actually carries. Present and empty where none were reported, so an empty answer and an absent field never read alike.

observed_tenant_id.description: WHICH DIRECTORY THIS SESSION OPERATED IN. Null, and it will stay null until something reads it from the session itself. IT MAY NEVER BE FILLED FROM `resolved_tenant_id`: that value is a lookup anybody can perform without ever reaching this tenant, and copying it here would make a public resolution indistinguishable from an observation — in the one field a reader trusts to mean what was seen.
